add-space-kinematics, design.md Decision 1 — Go is the SOLE authority for
continuous-space kinematics and there is no TypeScript mirror, now or later;
cross-stack-determinism › 'A Go-sole-authority capability's mirror map runs in
anti-mirror mode').
This file is the INVERSE of fixtures/market/mirror-map.json, the capability's
one remaining mirrored-pair map. That one asserts a mirror EXISTS and is covered.
This one asserts a mirror does NOT exist: .claude/scripts/check-mirror-map.sh's
anti_mirror_space pass fails if any function name is declared in BOTH
backend/space and frontend/lib/space unless it is listed in 'sharedNames'.
There is deliberately no 'pairs' array — a pairs entry would assert the very
mirror this capability exists to forbid.
'sharedNames' is empty BY DEFAULT and should stay that way. Adding a name here
is a claim that a render-side function may legitimately share a name with an
authoritative Go one; it needs the same scrutiny as a spec change.
frontend/lib/space does not exist as of this change (tasks.md 2.2 records that
omission as deliberate: the Go package has zero consumers, so there is no render
surface yet to draw). frontend/app/spike/space-3d is NEVER scanned — it is the
exempt, non-shipping feel bench named in space-kinematics › 'Every Rule-Bearing
Value of This Capability Is Computed Only in the Authoritative Implementation'.
'coverage' below is this capability's COVERAGE INVENTORY (tasks.md 3.9): every
function declared in backend/space, reconciled against the fixture families in
fixtures/space/cases.json. Values: 'family:<name>' — asserted by that family,
directly or indirectly as a callee of the family's function; 'inventory' — no
family exercises it, tracked as a gap in 'inventory' below.

inventory.why: Upkeep is a closed-form product of a body-derived rate and elapsed world time, unit-tested in park_test.go (the floor, the ordering of an inner vs an outer body, and read-count independence over 500 sub-intervals). migrate-fleet-to-continuous-burns (link 4) ships no station-keep currency — parks arise only from burn insertion (ParkOrbit) and stop-in-place (ParkPoint) — so the rate stays computable, not rule-bearing, through that change. Re-filed per Decision 17 (a rule-bearing shared function SHALL NOT remain in the inventory across more than one change that modifies backend/space) rather than carried forward unchanged.

Covered by three hand-selected parkPosition cases (the (3,2,4) planar re-circularization, the directly-above minimum-radius case, and the released park evaluated later) but by no randomized sweep, so an offset distribution it mishandles could still hide. add-fuel-as-cargo (link 7) is where a player-initiated release first has a caller, but it also settles the 2026-08-29 fleet-stranding ruling's guardrail: station-keeping upkeep SHALL NOT drain a fleet to zero, so when upkeep cannot be paid the park force-demotes to orbit, the free mode. That force-demote-to-orbit path is this function's first release path, ahead of any player-initiated release verb.

RESOLVED by migrate-fleet-to-continuous-burns (link 4, tasks.md 1.5) as DELETE, not give-a-caller: this change is 'the change that first migrates a consumer onto backend/space' the original entry named, and it gives backend/space's rule-bearing functions (SolveBurn, StateAt, etc.) their first PRODUCTION caller (fleet) — but no new production caller for this specific wrapper. Its only references anywhere were backend/space/fixtures_test.go's two star-clearance checks (sweepSolveBurn, sweepRealisticTraffic), both re-pointed to call the surviving minDistanceAndParamOf directly (discarding the curve-parameter component they do not need). The wrapper has since been deleted from backend/space/burn.go and its doc comment folded into minDistanceAndParamOf. minDistanceAndParamOf itself needs no separate fixture family — it is already swept via buildCurve's star-clearance axis.
